# 1.2.34 - the chrome face was never on screen, and the nine things seen on Forge

**The font.** The two VT323 files shipped since 1.2.29 were the wrong subsets:
the "Regular" file was Google's latin-ext subset (no A-Z, no digits), the
"LatinExt" file a third subset again. The browser reported both as loaded and
drew every letter from the next face in the list - Press Start 2P, more than
twice as wide - so the whole chrome of the theme has been rendered in a face
it was never sized for. That is most of "the label is cut": the hour, the
tray's names, the brush's label, the tiles' captions. Both files are now the
subsets Google Fonts serves (latin, latin-ext), checked glyph by glyph.

**The nine, in the order reported.**

- The GM launcher is centred under the clock, its own width (72 px at least,
  32 tall), the audit page's red brush with a Bone label; the base sheet had
  stretched it across the clock's pane. The seam between its pane and the
  clock's stays 10 px off either block.
- Seams: the self-check confirms every block's four corners on its own pane
  and no other, at 100 % and 140 %. Foundry's tiles were the exception - see
  below.
- Plates: Foundry's scene-control menus, the sidebar's tab rail and the
  player list stand clear on the glass; the tray's portrait squares are gone
  (a glyph takes their place).
- The Projects tray as drawn: the heading in the state colour, then per
  project a 16 px hourglass, the name, a halftone bar filled to its progress
  (projects-ui.mjs writes each row's share as `--w`), the count in Bone Dim.
- A window's band is the curtain's glass: the base sheet's Bone header under
  the canvas (`!important`, out of the theme's reach until now), the window's
  own ground and an additive seam glow the curtain does not have were the
  three reasons a band read brighter. Same material, same paint. Dialog
  titles are titles now: Special Elite at 21 px, not 11 px uppercase chrome.
- The tiles: the shard was cut around the rail's box, which carries the
  padding that pushes the rail under the clock - so the shard began far above
  the tiles and the rail turned about the wrong centre. It is cut around the
  tiles themselves and pivots on their centre. A short side strip keeps the
  tiles' shard without a mid seam instead of being dropped.
- The brush keeps off the letters: the button is as tall as its label,
  nothing in it clips, 14 px of padding, the brush starting 4 px outside the
  box so the tear lands on the straight edge.
- The campaign name is the clock's title: 21 px, with two steps for a long
  name (19, 17), and it may take two lines.
- The hour: the slot clips only while a turn-over is running, and hud.mjs
  measures the slot's width again whenever the font it measured in changes
  (the theme, the scale) instead of once per session.

`audit/glass-harness.html` now mirrors Foundry's own layout (one flex column
for the clock, the launcher and the scene controls; Daggerheart's tray
markup; a dialog and a popup) and takes `?scale=`, `?still=` and `?theme=`.
`drpgGlassDebug()` lists every pane and the tiles' shards.
